Ship as fast as you build

Run Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode in an open-source cloud, where review loops auto-approve the pull requests that pass your policy.

Get startedView source code

01 Code review

Code review that can auto-approve.

A pull request takes minutes to open and days to review. 143 reviews each PR with several coding agents and approves it on GitHub when it passes your policy.

Tune the policy. Pick the reviewer models.

Approval follows a policy you control: size limits, sensitive paths, required checks. The reviewers are coding agents, not people. Run one model to keep costs down, or several in parallel for confidence.

  • · Tune thresholds, sensitive paths, and required checks
  • · Raise the auto-approval rate by tightening policy
  • · Choose reviewer models: Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode
  • · Set reasoning depth per reviewer to control cost
Configure the review policy

02 Any agent

Run any coding agent.

Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Amp, and Pi each run in an isolated cloud sandbox. Connect an agent once and anyone on the team can start a run from the web, Slack, Linear, or Sentry.

  • · One isolated sandbox per run
  • · Team-visible sessions and transcripts
  • · Cheaper models for routine work
  • · Existing subscriptions used before metered billing

03 Previews

Preview every change in the cloud.

Every agent change can launch a browser preview from its sandbox, so teammates can check behavior before it reaches a PR.

  • · Shareable preview links
  • · Preview status in the session
  • · Browser checks before review
  • · No local setup required

04 Workspace

See every run in one workspace.

Sessions, previews, PR state, usage, and audit logs are visible to the whole team. Repair loops fix failing checks before anyone is asked to review. Engineers keep full control, and builders get scoped workflows.

05 Integrations

Connect your engineering tools.

Connect each tool once for the organization. Every agent starts with the same context your team already uses.

GitHub

Repos, branches, pull requests, and review state.

Linear

Issues, projects, priorities, and automation triggers.

Slack

Team notifications and job kickoff from conversation.

Sentry

Errors, traces, stack context, and production signals.

PagerDuty

Incidents and on-call alerts that kick off a fix.

Notion

Product notes, specs, runbooks, and team knowledge.

CircleCI

Build status, failing jobs, and repair-loop feedback.

Mezmo

Production log search and signals from Mezmo.

Put your agents to work.

Connect a repository, request 143 Code Reviewer on a pull request, and changes that pass your policy get approved automatically.
